home.titleLine2: Open source, ready out of the box
home.lead: DNS and NAT traversal, reverse proxy and HTTPS certificates, WAF and intrusion prevention, single sign-on and file sharing: everything your home network and servers need at the edge, managed from one console. Run it on a NAS, a soft router or a cloud server and set it all up in your browser.
home.featuresTitle: Everyday network tools, ready to go
home.featuresDesc: From pointing a domain at your home to guarding a whole row of websites, it all happens in one interface.

features.title: Dynamic DNS
features.text: Major providers including Alibaba Cloud, Cloudflare, Tencent Cloud, DNSPod, Huawei Cloud, Route 53, OVH, Gandi and Namecheap; detect your IP by URL, network interface or command, IPv4 and IPv6, webhook notifications.

features.title: STUN Traversal
features.text: TCP / UDP hole punching and keep-alive, UPnP / NAT-PMP, built-in forwarding; triggers webhooks and scripts when the public address changes.

features.title: Port Forwarding
features.text: TCP / UDP, IPv4 / IPv6, port ranges, multi-target failover, connection limits and traffic statistics; can send the PROXY protocol downstream to preserve the real client address; SNI routing lets several services share port 443.

features.title: SSL Certificates
features.text: Automatic ACME issuance and renewal with DNS-01 (including wildcards), HTTP-01 and EAB, plus short-lived and IP address certificates; map certificates to a directory and run a script after changes.

features.title: Web Services
features.text: Per-domain reverse proxy, redirects and static files; HTTPS, HTTP/3, WebSocket and PROXY protocol; weighted multi-backend policies, health checks, compression, rate limiting and response caching; can stand in for nginx: path backends, forward auth, and shared users with TOTP and single sign-on, plus a built-in OIDC identity provider.

features.title: WAF Firewall
features.text: Built-in Coraza and OWASP CRS v4, rules enabled per file, custom SecLang support, block or detect-only mode.

features.title: Networking & Tunnels
features.text: Supervises Tailscale, frp (frpc / frps) and cloudflared tunnels as managed processes, with online install, update, rollback and uninstall.

features.title: Docker Management
features.text: Create and edit containers, logs and terminals, Compose, image updates with one-click upgrade (automatic rollback on failure), networks and volumes.

features.title: Web Terminal
features.text: SSH, Telnet and a local shell (disabled by default) with proxy support, persistent sessions, SFTP file management and split panes.

features.title: File Services
features.text: WebDAV, FTP and SMB services, File Browser, and storage mounts for local directories, remote WebDAV and SMB shares, with online file management.

features.title: Scheduled Tasks & Wake-on-LAN
features.text: Cron jobs that run commands or HTTP requests and keep run history; Wake-on-LAN magic packet broadcast and online probing.

features.title: Security Hardening
features.text: Passkey and two-factor authentication, read-only accounts, audit log, config history with one-click rollback, login rate limiting, secure entrance path and LAN-only access.

features.title: Access Control
features.text: Per-site path rules, temporary share links, automatic bans on repeated auth failures, GeoIP country filtering and IP allow/block lists.

features.title: Traffic Stats & Monitoring
features.text: Global Prometheus metrics and a Grafana dashboard covering certificates, DDNS, port forwarding and sites; a one-click network self-check for NAT, ports, clock and DNS resolution.

features.title: Notification Center
features.text: Webhook, Telegram, Bark, ntfy, Gotify, Pushover, Discord, Slack, ServerChan, PushPlus, WeCom, DingTalk, Feishu and email; built-in rule templates, with silencing and de-duplication.

features.title: Configuration Backup
features.text: Encrypted backups (scrypt + AES-GCM), retention policies and scheduled backups to a local directory or a storage mount.

features.title: Network Diagnostics
features.text: Ping, traceroute, port probing, DNS lookup, speed test and LAN scan, all run as background tasks.

features.title: API, CLI & MCP
features.text: Multiple tokens with per-module permissions and auto-generated OpenAPI docs; use gately ctl to drive an instance and gately mcp to connect AI assistants.

features.title: Intrusion Prevention
features.text: fail2ban-style log jails, trap ports and scan detection, and bans for web path probing; bans sync to nftables and are dropped in the kernel.

fnos.title: On fnOS? Install and open
fnos.desc: Offline packages for x86 and ARM, installed manually from the App Center. Open it from the fnOS desktop through the fnOS unified gateway, and administrators already signed in to fnOS go straight in.

points.title: Through the fnOS unified gateway
points.text: Click the icon on the fnOS desktop and the admin UI opens under /app/gately/. Both the LAN address and your remote fnOS domain work, with no extra port to open or forward, and fnOS handles access control.

points.title: No second sign-in for fnOS admins
points.text: Turn on Sign in with fnOS and administrators already signed in to fnOS go straight into Gately, without a password or two-step code. Regular fnOS users still sign in. Off by default.

points.title: Every feature, running natively
points.text: Runs as root, so it can listen on 80/443, manage Docker and open the Web terminal. Config is kept on uninstall, and upgrading is installing the newer .fpk.

home.installDesc: Images are available for amd64, arm64 and arm/v7. After starting, open http://DEVICE_IP:16680 and sign in with the default account admin and default password gately.cn, then change the password right away.
home.installBinary:
# Download the archive for your platform from Releases and extract it
./gately -c /etc/gately

# The admin UI listens on :16680 by default
# Default account admin, default password gately.cn
home.installFnos:
# 1. Download gately_<version>_fnos_x86.fpk from Releases (_arm.fpk for ARM devices)
# 2. In fnOS, open App Center → Manual install, pick the file and finish the wizard
# 3. Click the Gately icon on the fnOS desktop to open it through the unified gateway

# Default account admin, default password gately.cn
home.installOpenwrt:
# 1. Check the device architecture, then download the matching OpenWrt package from Releases
grep DISTRIB_ARCH /etc/openwrt_release

# 2. Install (x86_64 as an example)
cd /tmp
# OpenWrt 24.10 / iStoreOS
opkg install ./gately_<version>_openwrt_amd64.ipk
# OpenWrt 25.12
apk add --allow-untrusted ./gately_<version>_openwrt_amd64.apk

# Gately starts right away; the admin UI is at http://ROUTER_IP:16680
# Optional: add luci-app-gately to manage it under Services → Gately in LuCI
# Default account admin, default password gately.cn

faqs.q: Does it need to connect to your servers?
faqs.a: No. Gately does not connect to any project servers by default and reports nothing.

faqs.q: Which devices can it run on?
faqs.a: Home NAS, soft routers, cloud hosts and servers of all kinds. Binaries are provided for Linux (amd64 / arm64 / arm / mips / mipsle / riscv64), macOS, Windows and FreeBSD, plus Docker images for amd64 / arm64 / arm/v7, a native app package for fnOS, and OpenWrt packages (.ipk / .apk).

Yes. Every release ships offline fnOS packages (.fpk) that you install manually from the App Center. Gately plugs into the fnOS unified gateway, so it opens from the desktop icon and also works over your remote fnOS domain. Turn on Sign in with fnOS under Settings → Access control and fnOS administrators who are signed in go straight in, without a password or two-step code.

faqs.q: Why is host networking recommended for port forwarding and STUN?
faqs.a: These modules listen directly on host ports. If you do not need Docker management, you can drop the docker.sock mount.

home.finalDesc: Free, open source and ready once installed. Questions? Find us in the Telegram group.
home.telegramScan: Scan with your phone to join the Telegram group

why.title: Why Gately
why.desc: Every point below is a feature you can use today.

items.title: Open and transparent
items.text: Apache-2.0 licensed. No connections to project servers by default, and nothing is collected or reported.

items.title: All in one
items.text: DDNS, traversal, reverse proxy, certificates, WAF, networking, Docker and file services in one console.

items.title: Layered security
items.text: WAF, intrusion bans, IP and country rules, single sign-on and two-factor auth, configured per site.

items.title: Audit log
items.text: Sign-ins, config changes and access to sensitive content are recorded, so you can see who did what and when.

items.title: Config rollback
items.text: Every change keeps the previous version. Compare the diff and restore it in one click.

items.title: Complete API
items.text: The admin UI runs on the same REST API. Tokens are scoped per module, with OpenAPI docs, a CLI and MCP.

items.title: Mobile friendly
items.text: The admin UI has a dedicated phone layout, so you can check status and change settings on the go.

items.title: Ready out of the box
items.text: One command or one package gets it running, and everything is set up in the browser.

showcase.title: See your whole network edge in one place
showcase.text: The overview shows host resources, network interfaces and public addresses, plus the state of every module, so you know at once what needs attention.
points: Port forwarding, DDNS, certificates and web services on one screen
One-click network self-check: public IP, CGNAT, ports, DNS and certificates
Prometheus metrics and a ready-made Grafana dashboard

showcase.title: Checks at every layer, from site to kernel
showcase.text: Each site can enable its own WAF, IP rules and sign-in. Intrusion prevention bans offenders from log rules and syncs them to the system firewall.
points: Coraza + OWASP CRS v4, blocking or detection only
fail2ban-style bans dropped in the kernel through nftables
Shared users, two-factor auth and OIDC single sign-on

showcase.title: Every change leaves a trail
showcase.text: Sign-ins, config changes and access to sensitive content go into the audit log. Overwritten config files keep their previous versions, with a diff and one-click rollback.
points: The audit log never records request bodies or secrets
Plain JSON config you can keep in git

showcase.title: Anything the UI does, the API does too
showcase.text: The admin UI itself is built on the REST API. Tokens get read-only or read-write access per module, and the built-in OpenAPI docs make scripting easy.
points: Multiple tokens, each with its own permissions and expiry
gately ctl drives a running instance from the command line
gately mcp connects AI assistants, read-only by default

showcase.title: Comfortable to manage from your phone
showcase.text: Navigation, lists and forms are laid out again for small screens. Open the same address in your phone's browser to check status and change settings.
points: Works in the phone browser, no app to install
Light, dark and several color themes
Multilingual UI that follows your browser language
